clue.text: About time reveal each poll broadcast is confused

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the short piece for time
seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, fourteen letters to rearrange
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A grumble that a pollster's televised results are muddled, and it's about time someone said so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time' reads as an exasperated aside, but 'About' wraps the rearranged letters round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all over the place is disorganised and muddled, an idiom for confused.

clue.text: Adult rugby player, huge incidentally

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for very large

explanation.surface: A grown-up rugby forward who happens to be enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used as an adverb, introduces a remark by the way, a synonym for incidentally.

clue.text: Plant many hedges for all to see

indicators.note: to hedge something is to surround it, as a hedge encloses a field

parts.note: lots means a great many
U is the British film certificate for a film suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A shrub planted in great numbers as a hedge that everybody can admire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the noun being defined. U is the universal film classification.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flowering aquatic plant.

clue.text: Sporting arena, very old ground outside European capital

indicators.note: outside signals that one piece wraps round the other, here the European capital split around the jumbled word

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters of old, mixed
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A stadium built on very old ground on the edge of a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: After V, the jumbled OLD sits between E and ROME; the setter treats 'European capital' as E plus ROME closing round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is a stadium with a banked track for cycle racing, so a sporting arena.

clue.text: Favour wine, dry, before starter of escalopes

parts.note: rosé is pink wine
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

indicators.note: the starter is the opening course, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of escalopes

explanation.surface: Choosing a dry wine to go before an escalope starter at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' looks like a verb about preferring the wine; it is a noun, a ribbon badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a rosette or knot of ribbon worn as a badge, e.g. at a wedding or by supporters.

clue.text: Replace extremely deficient setter, maybe ashamed

indicators.note: lacking at the extremes means both end letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: to change something is to replace it
a setter is a breed of dog; maybe flags an example

explanation.surface: Swap out a hopeless crossword setter, who might well feel ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' reads as the crossword compiler, but it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and guilty, the expression of someone ashamed.

clue.text: Present piano you said Trump scratched at intervals

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly

indicators.note: said means we take the spoken sound of you, not its spelling

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like you

indicators.note: scratching out every other letter leaves the ones at regular gaps

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of Trump

explanation.surface: Someone tells a pianist to give a present to Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a candidate or a proposal is to present or offer it.

clue.text: Clubman Dicky visiting A&E in this?

definitions.text: Clubman Dicky visiting A&E in this?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so these letters are placed within the hospital department

parts.note: the two letters of the emergency department's name

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the word's letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A clubman feeling poorly heads to Accident and Emergency, and the question is how he got there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: an ailing clubman might well reach A&E by this vehicle. Dicky is British slang for unwell or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance is the vehicle that carries the sick to hospital emergency departments.

clue.text: Heading off downcast, forced out

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off says it is taken away

parts.note: dejected means downcast and gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone leaves feeling low after being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejected means expelled or thrown out, the same as forced out.

clue.text: Recalled celebrity purchasing half of little child's toys

indicators.note: purchasing means taking in and holding, so one piece goes inside the other
recalled is read as called back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word keeps just three of its letters, here the back half

parts.note: the second half of little

explanation.surface: A remembered celebrity buys some baby toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattles are noisy toys shaken by babies and toddlers.

clue.text: Distinguished student amongst English staff returning

indicators.note: amongst places the student among the other pieces, inside them
returning means going back, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
L is a learner driver's plate, so a student
a baton is a short staff or stick

explanation.surface: An eminent student is among the English faculty staff who come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means worthy of note, eminent, a synonym for distinguished.

clue.text: Delivery of letters old-fashioned, like cheques might be?

parts.note: the post is the delivery of mail
dated means out of fashion

explanation.surface: Letters still arriving by post seems as old-fashioned as paying by cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a cheque can carry a future date so it cannot be cashed yet.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdated cheque bears a date later than the day it is written, delaying payment.

clue.text: Airline employee, one involved in conspiracy

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so this piece is set within the other

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An airline worker is caught up in a sinister conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies the aircraft, a central member of an airline's staff.

clue.text: Fancy having drink with model

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a model poses for an artist
with simply joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: Do you fancy having a drink with a model?
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to imagine or think it, the same as suppose.

clue.text: Flirt with former occupants of Buckingham Palace?

parts.note: Phil is Prince Philip, one of the late royal couple
with means and, in addition
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen and the other former resident

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with the royals who used to live at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal couple is spelt Phil and ER, the 'with' landing between them; ER is Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to womanise or have casual affairs, the verb flirt in a stronger sense.

clue.text: Complained when going round friend Ena or Gail's houses

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the run of letters is read backwards
houses means contains, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters running across friend Ena or Gail

explanation.surface: Someone moaned while visiting the houses of their friends Ena and Gail.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena and Gail are Coronation Street characters, the long-running British TV soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Groaned means moaned or complained, as one does when grumbling.

clue.text: More able to support unfashionable clothing seller

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
fitter means more able or healthier

explanation.surface: A better shop to support is one selling unfashionable clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, to support means to sit under, so the second piece goes below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or trader selling clothes, especially for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Emojis messily replaced

indicators.note: replaced means put back in different places, so the letters change position

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone's emojis have been swapped in a careless way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messily' sounds like the adverb modifying replaced, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Smileys are smiling-face symbols, the original kind of emoji.

clue.text: Detectives right to flee ruthless criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the remaining letters are bent into a new order
something that flees runs away, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Detectives let a ruthless criminal escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleuths is an informal word for detectives, from sleuth-hound, a tracking dog.

clue.text: Hide from opponents on island

parts.note: South and East sit as opponents at the bridge table
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Hiding out from enemies on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points; any two adjacent ones, such as S and E, are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, so to hide.

clue.text: Vegetable broth cooked with peas since discarded

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are mixed up
something discarded is thrown away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
as can mean since, because

explanation.surface: A recipe: a vegetable broth cooked with peas, which have since been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-herb is any plant whose leaves or stems are boiled as a vegetable.

clue.text: Work over, books provided comfort essentially for bishop

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the short word is flipped back to front

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
if means provided that

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so the central letter is used

parts.note: middle letter of comfort

explanation.surface: A bishop is given comfort by working through books.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiff is a title of a bishop, especially the Pope as Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Implore discontented employees to cut wood

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, splitting it

parts.note: beech is a hardwood

indicators.note: with its contents removed a word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: outer letters of employees

explanation.surface: Unhappy workers pleading to be allowed to fell the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg earnestly, so to implore.

clue.text: Coat shorn repeatedly from Icelandic animal

indicators.note: shearing the outer coat again and again strips the outside letters, layer after layer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fleece clipped again and again from an Icelandic sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Two layers come off each end of the nine-letter word, leaving its core.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, an animal.

clue.text: Peach-like fruit reportedly showing wilt

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the sound counts

parts.note: a drupe is a stone fruit such as a peach

explanation.surface: A peach-like fruit starting to wilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or hang down limply, which is what a wilting plant does.

clue.text: Persuades departments to sack expert after scam

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: to sack someone is to dismiss them, so that word is removed

parts.note: French départements are administrative provinces
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: Government departments are persuaded to fire an expert after a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To convince someone is to persuade them that something is true.

clue.text: Dance about grabbing leg, aching ultimately

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the outer piece wraps the others

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
the on side is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: last letter of aching

explanation.surface: A dancer grabs a leg that is finally aching.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a long single-file line.

clue.text: Young swimmer a little ahead of Rod

parts.note: a tad means a little bit
a pole is a rod

explanation.surface: A young swimmer just ahead of a rival named Rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' is capitalised to look like a person's name; it is a plain rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog's larva, a young creature that swims before growing legs.

clue.text: Great plans spending day close to seaside

indicators.note: spending something uses it up, so that letter is lost

parts.note: intends means plans
D is the abbreviation for day

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of seaside

explanation.surface: Fantastic holiday plans: spending the day by the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means great in degree or extreme, as in intense heat.

clue.text: Poor son Johnny maybe guards captured female soldiers

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so the outer letters enclose the rest

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
Johnny Cash, the American singer; maybe flags an example
trapped means captured
F is the abbreviation for female
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A hard-up son, perhaps named Johnny, stands guard over women soldiers taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnny' looks like the son's name, but it is the surname-giver: Johnny Cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped for cash is an idiom for short of money, so poor.
